Definition: Baal-Chanan, the name of an Edomite, also of an Israelite
BiblicalUsage: Baal-hanan is the name of two men — a king of Edom who reigned after Saul of Rehoboth, whose death is recorded in Genesis and Chronicles alike, and an overseer of David's olive trees and sycamores in the low plains. A king and a gardener, both remembered, both named Baal-hanan.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God records kings and gardeners in the same book, because the olive trees mattered to David's kingdom as much as the throne did.
